Each scenario's code is the body of an async function of `env` ({ locks, log, turn, show, gate }); the test runs the same code against the fast path's lock manager.

scenarios.name: exclusive: the callback gets the lock and its result is the request's
scenarios.code:
const seen = []; const p = env.locks.request("a", lock => { seen.push([lock.name, lock.mode, Object.prototype.toString.call(lock), Object.keys(lock), JSON.stringify(lock)]); return 42; });
    env.log("sync", seen.length, p instanceof Promise); env.log("result", await p, seen); env.log("after", await env.locks.query());

scenarios.name: exclusive: when the callback runs relative to the caller and microtasks
exclusive: requests for one name run one at a time in order
exclusive: different names do not wait for each other
shared: holders overlap, an exclusive waits for all of them and later shared requests wait behind it
ifAvailable: a held lock answers null at once, a free one is granted
ifAvailable: shared with shared is available, shared with exclusive or a waiting exclusive is not
steal: the holder's request rejects, the thief holds the lock and waiters stay queued
